units.text: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, so that the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians. He ordered a proclamation throughout his kingdom, also in writing, saying:
“Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build Him a house in Jerusalem in Judea.
Who among you belongs to any of His people? His God will be with him, and he will go up to Jerusalem in Judea. Let him build the house of the God of Israel—He is the God in Jerusalem.

As for everyone left behind, from whatever place he resides in, the men of his place will take him up with silver, gold, belongings and livestock, together with the freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.”
But now thus says the Lord God who made you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I redeemed you. I called you by your name; you are Mine.
Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not flood over you. Even if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; flame will not burn you up.
For I am the Lord your God, Israel’s Holy One, who saves you. I made Egypt your exchange, and Ethiopia and Soene on your behalf.
Since you became honored before Me, you were glorified, and I loved you. I will give many people on your behalf and rulers for your head.
Do not fear, for I am with you. From the east I will bring your offspring, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north, ‘Bring them,’ and to the southwest, ‘Do not hinder. Bring My sons from a distant land and My daughters from the earth’s extremities,
all who are called by My name.’ For in My glory I fashioned him, formed him, and made him,
and I brought out a blind people, and their eyes are likewise blind, and deaf people who have ears.

All nations were gathered together, and rulers from them will assemble. Who will announce these things, or who will announce to you the things from the beginning? Let them bring their witnesses, be justified, and speak true things.

Become witnesses for Me—and I too am a witness, says the Lord God, and the servant whom I chose—so that you may know, believe, and understand that I am. Before Me no other god came to be, nor will there be one after Me.
I am God, and apart from Me there is no one who saves.
I announced and saved; I reproached, and there was no foreign one among you. You are witnesses for Me, and I too am a witness, says the Lord God,
still from the beginning. No one rescues from My hands. I will act, and who will turn it back?”
But you, Israel, My servant Jacob whom I chose, offspring of Abraham whom I loved,
whom I took hold of from the earth’s extremities, and from its lookout heights called you and said, ‘You are My servant; I chose you and did not abandon you’—
do not fear, for I am with you; do not wander, for I am your God who strengthened you. I helped you and secured you with My righteous right hand.
That you might know that the Lord your God, He is God, and there is none beside Him.
Out of heaven His voice was made heard, to instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire.
Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, even you, and Himself brought you forth out of Egypt by His great strength,
to destroy nations great and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, and to give you their land to inherit, as you have this day.
And you shall know this day, and lay it to mind, that the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and upon earth beneath; there is none beside Him.

“For from the sun’s rising to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to My name, together with a pure sacrifice, because My name is great among the nations,” says the Lord Almighty.
Will a trumpet sound in a city and the people not be alarmed? Will there be calamity in a city that the Lord has not done?
In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
Now the earth was unseen and unformed, and darkness was over the deep; and the Spirit of God was moving over the water.
And God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
And God saw that the light was good, and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning: one day.
Nevertheless His salvation is near those who fear Him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
Mercy and truth met; righteousness and peace kissed.
Truth sprang up from the earth, and righteousness looked down from heaven.
For the Lord will also give goodness, and our land will give its fruit.
You will then say to me, “Why, then, does He still find fault? For who has resisted His purpose?”
But who are you, O man, to answer back to God? Will what is formed say to the One who formed it, “Why didst Thou make me this way?”
Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
But what if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
and did so to make known the wealth of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,

Esdras said, “Thou alone art the Lord. Thou madest heaven, the heaven of heaven and all their array, the earth and everything in it, the seas and everything in them. Thou givest life to all things, and the armies of heaven worship Thee.
But if everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or an uninitiated person enters, he is exposed by all, examined by all;
the hidden things of his heart are revealed, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God, declaring, “God is truly among you.”
For as I passed through and observed your objects of worship, I also found an altar inscribed, ‘To an unknown god.’ What you worship without knowing, this I proclaim to you.
The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands.
Nor is He served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything.
From one He made every nation of humanity to live upon the whole face of the earth, determining their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
so that they might seek God, if perhaps they might feel their way toward Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are His offspring.’
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
for He shattered bronze gates and broke iron bars.
Behold, all opposing you will be ashamed and abashed, for all your adversaries will be as though they did not exist and will perish.
You will seek them but certainly not find the people who insult you. For those warring against you will be as though they did not exist, and will not exist.
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own eyes: that a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles enters,
and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
Then the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and about His teaching.
Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in a synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I spoke nothing in secret.
Why do you question Me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them. See, these know what I said.”
Hear the Lord’s word that He spoke concerning you, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: Do not learn according to the nations’ ways, and do not fear heaven’s signs, because they fear them before their faces.
For the nations’ customs are futile: it is wood cut from the woodland, a carpenter’s work and a cast object.
They are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they fastened them, and they will not move.
They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.
It is worked silver; they will not walk. Applied silver will come from Tarshish, gold from Mophaz, and the goldsmiths’ hand; all are artisans’ works. They will dress them in blue and purple.
This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
The Lord who made the earth by His strength, who set the inhabited world upright by His wisdom, also stretched out heaven by His understanding,
and an abundance of water in heaven; and He brought clouds up from the earth’s extremity, made lightning for rain, and brought light out of His treasuries.
Every human became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame at his carved things, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them.
They are futile, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not such as this, because the One who formed everything is himself his inheritance; Lord is His name.
Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the divine nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human art and thought.
Therefore, having overlooked the times of ignorance, God now commands all people everywhere to repent,
because He has fixed a day on which He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness through a Man whom He appointed, giving assurance to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
But why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat,
for it is written, “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to Me, and every tongue will confess to God.”
So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
Therefore God also highly exalted Him and graciously gave Him the name above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
And we know that all things work together for good for those who love God, those who are called according to purpose.
Because those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He might be firstborn among many brothers;
and those whom He predestined, these He also called; and those whom He called, these He also justified; and those whom He justified, these He also glorified.
The foreigners took the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
The foreigners took the ark of the Lord, brought it into Dagon’s house, and placed it beside Dagon.

The Ashdodites rose early, entered Dagon’s house, and looked: there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of God. They raised Dagon and restored him to his place. The Lord’s hand became heavy upon the Ashdodites. He tormented them and struck them on their buttocks—Ashdod and its territory.

When they rose early in the morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the Lord’s covenant. Dagon’s head and both soles of his hands were severed, each upon the front parts of amapheth; both wrists of his hands had fallen at the doorway. Only Dagon’s back remained.
That is why Dagon’s priests and everyone entering Dagon’s house do not step on the step of Dagon’s house in Ashdod to this day: they always step over it.
And I said unto you: Neither cower nor fear them.
The Lord your God, who goes before you, shall Himself fight against them with you, according to all that He did for you in the land of Egypt,
and in this wilderness which you saw, how the Lord your God nurtured you as a man nurtures his son, in all the way which you went, until you came unto this place.
Thou didst teach me, God, from my youth, and until now I will announce Thy wonders.
And until old age and advanced years, God, do not forsake me, until I announce Thine arm to the whole coming generation, Thy power and Thy righteousness—
To whom did you liken the Lord, and to what likeness did you liken Him?
Did a craftsman make an image, or did a goldsmith melt gold and gild it, fashioning it as a likeness?
For a craftsman chooses wood that will not rot and skillfully seeks how to set up his image so that it will not shake.
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.

Many are the reasonings in a man’s heart, but the counsel of the Lord remains for ever.
Thus says the Lord: “Keep justice; do righteousness. For the coming of My salvation has drawn near, and the revealing of My mercy.
Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overturned Sodom and Gomorrah.
She will not be inhabited for everlasting time, nor will people ever enter her through many generations. Arabs will certainly not pass through her, and shepherds will certainly not rest in her.
Wild beasts will rest there, and the houses fill with sound; sirens will rest there, and demons dance there.
Donkey-centaurs will dwell there, and hedgehogs make nests in their houses. It comes quickly and will not delay.
The foreigners seized him and dug out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza, bound him with bronze fetters, and he ground grain in the prison house.
look, I am against you, says the Lord God Almighty. I will expose your hind parts over your face and show nations your shame and kingdoms your dishonor,
and cast abomination upon you according to your impurities, and make you an example,
Thus says the Lord God who redeems you, Israel’s Holy One: “For your sake I will send to Babylon and rouse all who flee, and Chaldeans will be bound in ships.
I am the Lord God, your Holy One, who presented Israel as your king.”
The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy,
and I am angry with great anger at the nations joining in assault, because I was a little angry, but they joined in attacking to bring evils.
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in compassion, and My house will be rebuilt in her, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure will again be extended over Jerusalem.”
The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Cities will again overflow with good things; the Lord will again have mercy on Zion and again choose Jerusalem.”
Her uncleanness is at her feet; she did not remember her last things. He brought her down exceedingly; there is no one to comfort her. See, Lord, my humiliation, for the enemy has grown great!

This is the contemptuous city dwelling in confidence, saying in her heart, “I am, and there is no one after me.” How she became a wasteland, pasture for wild animals! Everyone passing through her will hiss and wave his hands.
Their widows multiplied beyond the sea’s sand. I brought misery upon a young man’s mother at noon; suddenly I cast trembling and haste upon her.
She who bore seven was emptied; her soul grew faint. Her sun set while the day was still at its middle; she was ashamed and reproached. Their remnants I will give to the sword before their enemies.
The Chaldeans answered before the king, “No one on earth can tell the king what he has seen, as you ask. No king and no ruler asks such a thing of any wise man, magus, or Chaldean.

The matter you seek, O king, is weighty and extraordinary. No one can disclose these things to the king except perhaps an angel, whose dwelling is not with any flesh. Therefore it cannot happen as you suppose.”
Daniel spoke aloud before the king, “Disclosure of the mystery the king saw does not belong to wise men, sorcerers, incantation-singers, or gazarenes,

but there is a God in heaven who uncovers mysteries, who has disclosed to King Nebuchadnezzar what must happen in the last days. O king, live for ever! This is the dream and the vision of your head upon your bed:
The delusions of magical art lay prostrate, and its boasting of understanding suffered a scornful exposure;
for those who promised to drive away the terrors and disturbances of a sick soul were themselves sick with a ridiculous fear.
For it will be laid waste to their foundation, consumed like an entwining thorn-vine and like stubble full of dryness.
and swears, ‘The Lord lives,’ with truth and in judgment and righteousness, then nations will bless in her, and in Him they will praise God in Jerusalem.
Do not put your confidence in yourselves on false words, because they will not benefit you at all when they say, ‘The Lord’s temple, the Lord’s temple it is.’
For if you truly correct your ways and practices and truly execute judgment between a man and his neighbor,
and do not oppress a newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm,
then I will settle you in this place, in the land I gave your fathers, from age to age.
But if you have trusted false words from which you will receive no benefit,
and murder and commit adultery and steal and swear unjustly, and you burned incense to Baal and followed foreign gods whom you do not know, to your own harm,
and you came and stood before Me in the house over which My name has been called and said, ‘We have kept away, so as not to do all these abominations,’
And you shall know this day that the Lord your God does not give you this good land to inherit for your righteous deeds; for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day when you came forth out of Egypt until you came unto this place, you continued in disobedience toward the Lord.

Lord, Thine eyes are toward faithfulness. Thou didst scourge them, and they did not suffer; Thou broughtest them to an end, and they would not accept instruction. They hardened their faces beyond rock and would not return.
They entered the nations where they entered, and profaned My holy name when it was said of them, ‘These are the Lord’s people, and they have left His land.’
I spared them because of My holy name, which Israel’s house profaned among the nations where they entered.
Therefore say to Israel’s house, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am not acting for you, house of Israel, but because of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you entered.
I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
But God took you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be unto Him a people of inheritance, as at this day.
I am the Lord God; this is My name. I will not give My glory to another or My praiseworthy deeds to carved images.
Behold, the things from the beginning have arrived, and new things I will announce; before they spring up, they were disclosed to you.”
Make Thy ways known to me, Lord, and teach me Thy paths.
Guide me into Thy truth and teach me, for Thou art God my Savior, and I waited for Thee the whole day.
surely I will bless you, and greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand upon the shore of the sea; and your seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries.
I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long.”
Look, the angel speaking within me was standing, and another angel was going out to meet him,
And the Lord said to Moses, “Go before this people, and take with you some of the elders of the people; and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the river, and go.
Behold, I stand before you there upon the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come forth from it, and My people shall drink.” And Moses did so before the sons of Israel.
But the unjust will be tossed by waves in this way and will be unable to rest.
‘There is no rejoicing for the ungodly,’ said the Lord God.”
and said to him, “Run and speak to that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited fruitfully because of the multitude of people and animals within her.
I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”
“Oh! Oh! Flee from the northern land,” says the Lord, “because I will gather you from the four winds of heaven,” says the Lord.
Escape safely to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon!
For thus says the Lord Almighty: “After glory He has sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one touching the pupil of his eye.
Look, I am bringing My hand against them, and they will become spoils for those serving them; you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.”
“Delight and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell within you,” says the Lord.
Many nations will take refuge with the Lord on that day and become His people. They will dwell within you, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
The Lord will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy land and again choose Jerusalem.
Let all flesh be reverent before the Lord, for He has risen from His holy clouds.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
Before I formed you in the belly, I know you; before you came out of the womb, I have consecrated you. I have appointed you a prophet to nations.
I said, O Master Lord! Behold, I do not know how to speak, because I am young.
The Lord said to me, Do not say, I am young, because you will go to everyone to whom I send you, and you will speak according to everything I command you.
Do not fear them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.
The Lord stretched out His hand toward me and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, Behold, I have put My words into your mouth.
Behold, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant.

For the word of God is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword, penetrating as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
And no created thing is hidden before Him, but all things are naked and laid open to His eyes, to whom we must give account.
And receive the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, knowing that your labor is not empty in the Lord.

Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly and said, “It was necessary for God’s word to be spoken to you first. Since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look—we are turning to the Gentiles.
For the Lord has commanded us in this way: ‘I have appointed you as a light for Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the end of the earth.’”
When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
“Now, Master, Thou art releasing Thy servant in peace according to Thy word,
because my eyes have seen Thy salvation,
which Thou didst prepare in the sight of all peoples:
a light for revelation to the nations and glory for Thy people Israel.”
kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts; kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.

And working together, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain.

“I, the Lord God, called you in righteousness; I will hold your hand and strengthen you. I gave you as a covenant for a people, a light for nations,
to open blind people’s eyes, bring those bound out of bonds, and those sitting in darkness out of the prison house.
A psalm of David. The Lord shepherds me, and nothing shall fail me.
He made me dwell in a place of green growth; He nourished me beside water of rest.
He turned my soul back; He guided me upon paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.
For even if I walk in the midst of death’s shadow, I will fear no evils, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff comforted me.
Thou didst prepare a table before me opposite those who afflict me; Thou didst enrich my head with oil, and Thy cup is intoxicating—how excellent!
And Thy mercy will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the Lord’s house for length of days.
A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low; all the crooked places will become straight, and the rough country will become plains.
And the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God; for the Lord has spoken.
Rejoice, heavens, because God had mercy on Israel! Sound trumpets, earth’s foundations! Cry out joy, mountains, hills and all their trees! For God redeemed Jacob, and Israel will be glorified.
How long, Lord, wilt Thou forget me utterly? How long wilt Thou turn Thy face away from me?
For my father and my mother abandoned me, but the Lord took me to Himself.
I kept seeing the Lord before me continually, because He is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.
Lift your eyes around you and see your children gathered. Behold, all your sons have come from far away, and your daughters will be lifted upon shoulders.
Then you will see and fear and be astonished in heart, for the wealth of sea, nations, and peoples will turn toward you. There will come to you

and they will rejoice greatly in the Lord.” Let my soul exult in the Lord, for He clothed me in a garment of salvation and a tunic of joy. Like a bridegroom He placed a turban on me, and like a bride He adorned me with ornaments.
Destruction will come upon every city; no city will be saved. The valley will perish and the plain be destroyed, as the Lord said.
Give signs to Moab, for she will surely be kindled; all her cities will become an untrodden place. From where will an inhabitant come to her?
Accursed is one who does the Lord’s works carelessly, removing his sword from blood.
But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are at peace.
But when someone stronger than he attacks and defeats him, he takes away the full armor in which he trusted and distributes his spoils.
Behold, I am bringing them from the north and will gather them from the earth’s farthest end at the Passover festival. You will bear a great crowd, and they will return here.

They went out with weeping, and with encouragement I will bring them up, lodging them beside water channels on a straight road where they will certainly not wander, because I became Israel’s father, and Ephraim is My firstborn.
Hear the Lord’s word, nations, and announce it to the farther islands. Say: He who winnowed Israel will gather him and guard him like one tending his flock.
Foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will attend you. For because of My anger I struck you, and because of mercy I loved you.
Ethiopians will fall before him, and his enemies will lick dust.
kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts; kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.

The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to Me. They went upon every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree and prostituted themselves there.
After she prostituted herself in all these ways, I said, Return to Me. But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her faithlessness.

I saw that, concerning all the things in which the dwelling of Israel was caught committing adultery, I sent her away and gave a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet faithless Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
Is the Lord’s hand unable to save? Or has His ear grown heavy so that He cannot hear?
Instead, your offenses stand between you and God, and because of your sins He has turned His face away from you so as not to show mercy.
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded. He raised his staff and struck the river’s water before Pharaoh and his attendants, and all the water in the river turned to blood.
The fish in the river died, and the river stank. The Egyptians could not drink its water, and there was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness upon the land of Egypt, darkness that may be felt.”
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was darkness, gloom, and a tempest throughout the land of Egypt for three days.
No one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose from his bed for three days. But all the sons of Israel had light everywhere they lived.
All bore witness to Him and wondered at the words of grace coming from His mouth. They said, “Is this not Joseph’s son?”
So the Jews marveled, saying, “How does this man know the writings without having studied?”
So Jesus answered them, “My teaching is not Mine, but belongs to the One who sent Me.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
Then they spat into His face and struck Him with their fists; others slapped Him,
Then he released Barabbas to them; after flogging Jesus, he handed Him over to be crucified.
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around Him.
They stripped Him and put a scarlet cloak around Him.
They wove a crown from thorns, placed it upon His head, and put a reed in His right hand. Kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews!”
They spat on Him, took the reed, and kept striking Him upon the head.
As the days for His being taken up approached their fulfillment, He firmly set His face to go to Jerusalem.
What, then, shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
He who did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us all, how will He not also graciously give us all things with Him?
Who will bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? God is the One who justifies.
Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died—more than that, was raised—who is also at God’s right hand, who also intercedes for us.

Isaiah 45:15.text: for Thou art God, and we did not know it, Israel’s God, the Savior.’”

Isaiah 45:16.text: All who oppose Him will be ashamed and abashed and go away in shame. “Be renewed toward Me, islands.”

Isaiah 45:17.text: Israel is saved by the Lord with everlasting salvation. They will not be ashamed or ever be abashed for eternity.

Isaiah 45:18.text: Thus says the Lord who made heaven—He is the God who displayed the earth and made it, who marked it out; He did not make it for emptiness, but to be inhabited—“I am, and there is no other.

Isaiah 45:19.text: I have not spoken in secret or in a dark place of the earth. I did not say to Jacob’s offspring, ‘Seek a futile thing.’ I am, I am the Lord, speaking righteousness and announcing truth.

Isaiah 45:20.text: Gather and come; take counsel together, you who are saved from the nations. Those carrying wood as their carved image did not know, praying as though to gods who do not save.

Isaiah 45:21.text: If they will announce it, let them draw near so that they may know together who made these things heard from the beginning. Then it was announced to you: I am God, and there is no other besides Me; there is none righteous and saving apart from Me.

Isaiah 45:22.text: Turn back to Me, and you will be saved, you from the earth’s extremity. I am God, and there is no other.

Isaiah 45:23.text: By Myself I swear: Surely righteousness will go out from My mouth; My words will not return, because every knee will bend to Me and every tongue will confess to God,

Isaiah 45:24.text: saying, ‘Righteousness and glory will come to Him,’ and all who set themselves apart will be ashamed.

Isaiah 45:25.text: From the Lord all the offspring of Israel’s sons will be justified, and in God they will be glorified.”

Isaiah 46:1.text: Bel fell; Dagon was shattered. Their carved images became a burden for wild and domestic animals. Lift them, bound together, as a load for one who is weary

Isaiah 46:2.text: and hungry and exhausted, without strength at all; they cannot be saved from war, and they themselves were led captive.

Isaiah 46:3.text: “Listen to Me, house of Jacob and all Israel’s remnant, you who are carried from the belly and instructed from childhood.

Isaiah 46:4.text: Until old age I am, and until you grow very old I am. I bear with you; I made you, and I will release you. I will take you up and save you.

Isaiah 46:5.text: To whom did you liken Me? Look, devise your handiwork, you who wander astray.

Isaiah 46:6.text: Those contributing gold from a pouch will set silver on a balance by weight; after hiring a goldsmith they made handmade objects and bend down to worship them.

Isaiah 46:7.text: They lift it onto their shoulders and go along. If they set it down, it stays in its place and will never move. Whoever cries to it, it will certainly not listen or save him from evils.

Isaiah 46:8.text: Remember these things and groan. Repent, you who have wandered astray; turn back in heart.

Isaiah 46:9.text: Remember the former things from eternity, for I am God, and there is none besides Me,

Isaiah 46:10.text: announcing the last things beforehand, before they came to be—and together they were fulfilled. I said, ‘All My counsel will stand, and I will do everything I have planned,’

Isaiah 46:11.text: calling a bird from the east and from a distant land concerning what I have planned. I spoke and brought it about; I created and acted. I brought him and made his journey prosper.

Isaiah 46:12.text: Listen to Me, you who have lost heart, who are far from righteousness.

Isaiah 46:13.text: I brought My righteousness near, and I will not delay the salvation that comes from Me. I have given salvation in Zion to Israel for glory.”

Isaiah 47:1.text: “Come down and sit on the ground, virgin daughter Babylon. Enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for you will no longer be called tender and pampered.

Isaiah 47:2.text: Take a millstone and grind flour. Uncover your veil, expose your gray hair, pull up your garments to bare your lower legs, and cross rivers.

Isaiah 47:3.text: Your shame will be uncovered, and your reproaches will be visible. I will exact justice from you; I will certainly no longer hand it over to humans.”

Isaiah 47:4.text: The One who rescued you said—His name is the Lord Sabaoth, Israel’s Holy One—

Isaiah 47:5.text: “Sit stricken and enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will certainly no longer be called a kingdom’s strength.

Isaiah 47:6.text: I was provoked against My people; you defiled My inheritance. I gave it into your hand, but you gave them no mercy; you made the elder’s yoke exceedingly heavy.

Isaiah 47:7.text: You said, ‘I will rule for ever.’ You did not consider these things in your heart or remember the last things.

Isaiah 47:8.text: Now hear these things, pampered one who sits confident, saying in her heart, ‘I am, and there is no other. I will not sit as a widow or know bereavement.’

Isaiah 47:9.text: Now these two will come upon you suddenly, in one day: widowhood and childlessness will come suddenly upon you, amid your sorcery and the overwhelming power of your enchanters,

Isaiah 47:10.text: in your hope of wickedness. For you said, ‘I am, and there is no other.’ Know that understanding these things and your prostitution will become your shame. You said in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no other.’

Isaiah 47:11.text: Destruction will come upon you, and you will certainly not know it—a pit, and you will fall into it. Misery will come upon you, and you will certainly not be able to become clean. Destruction will come upon you suddenly, and you will certainly not know it.

Isaiah 47:12.text: Stand now amid your enchantments and your abundant sorcery, which you learned from youth, if you can be helped.

Isaiah 47:13.text: You have toiled in your counsels. Let heaven’s astrologers stand up and save you; let those watching the stars announce to you what is about to come upon you.

Isaiah 47:14.text: Behold, all will be burned up like brushwood upon a fire and certainly not rescue their soul from flame. Since you have burning coals, sit upon them!

Isaiah 47:15.text: These will be your help! You toiled in your trade from youth; each person wandered on his own, but there will be no salvation for you.”

Isaiah 48:1.text: “Hear these things, house of Jacob, you called by Israel’s name, who came forth from Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord God of Israel, remembering without truth or righteousness,

Isaiah 48:2.text: and cling to the holy city’s name and lean upon Israel’s God; His name is the Lord Sabaoth.

Isaiah 48:3.text: I announced the former things beforehand; they went out from My mouth and were heard. Suddenly I acted, and they arrived.

Isaiah 48:4.text: I know that you are stubborn, your neck an iron sinew and your forehead bronze.

Isaiah 48:5.text: I announced it to you long ago; before it came upon you I made you hear it. Do not say, ‘My idols did it,’ or say, ‘My carved and cast images commanded me.’

Isaiah 48:6.text: You heard everything, but you did not understand. Yet I also made you hear the new things from now on, what is about to happen, and you did not speak.

Isaiah 48:7.text: They happen now, not long ago; you did not hear them in earlier days. Do not say, ‘Yes, I know them.’

Isaiah 48:8.text: You neither knew nor understood; from the beginning I did not open your ears. For I knew you would utterly reject faithfulness, and you would be called lawless even from the belly.

Isaiah 48:9.text: For My name’s sake I will show you My anger and bring My glorious deeds upon you, so that I do not destroy you.

Isaiah 48:10.text: Behold, I sold you, but not for silver; I rescued you from a furnace of poverty.

Isaiah 48:11.text: For My sake I will act for you, because My name is being profaned. I will not give My glory to another.

Isaiah 48:12.text: Listen to Me, Jacob and Israel whom I call. I am first, and I am for ever,

Isaiah 48:13.text: and My hand founded the earth, and My right hand established heaven. I will call them, and they will stand together

Isaiah 48:14.text: and all will gather and hear. Who announced these things to them? Loving you, I carried out your will against Babylon, to remove the Chaldeans’ offspring.

Isaiah 48:15.text: I spoke, I called; I brought him and made his journey prosper.

Isaiah 48:16.text: Draw near to Me and hear these things. From the beginning I did not speak in secret or in a dark place of the earth. When it came to be, I was there; and now the Lord has sent me, and His spirit.”

Isaiah 48:17.text: Thus says the Lord who rescued you, Israel’s Holy One: “I am your God. I have shown you how to find the road on which you will walk.

Isaiah 48:18.text: If you had listened to My commands, your peace would have become like a river and your righteousness like a sea wave.

Isaiah 48:19.text: Your offspring would have become like sand, those born from your belly like the earth’s dust. Even now you will certainly not be destroyed, nor will your name perish before Me.”

Isaiah 48:20.text: Leave Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans. Announce a voice of rejoicing, and let this be heard; proclaim it to the earth’s extremity. Say, “The Lord rescued His slave Jacob.”

Isaiah 48:21.text: Even if they thirst, He will lead them through a wilderness and bring water out of a rock for them. A rock will split and water will flow, and My people will drink.

Isaiah 48:22.text: “There is no rejoicing for the ungodly,” says the Lord.

Isaiah 49:1.text: Listen to me, islands, and attend, nations. “After a long time it will stand,” says the Lord. From my mother’s belly He called my name,

Isaiah 49:2.text: and made my mouth like a sharp sword. In the shelter of His hand He hid me; He made me a chosen arrow and sheltered me in His quiver.

Isaiah 49:3.text: He said to me, “You are My slave, Israel, and in you I will be glorified.”

Isaiah 49:4.text: I said, “I toiled in vain and gave my strength to futility and nothing. Therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my toil before my God.”

Isaiah 49:5.text: And now thus says the Lord, who formed me from the belly as His slave to gather Jacob and Israel to Him—I will be gathered and glorified before the Lord, and my God will be my strength—

Isaiah 49:6.text: and He said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called My servant, to establish Jacob’s tribes and bring back Israel’s dispersion. Behold, I have appointed you as a covenant for a race, a light for nations, so that you may bring salvation to the earth’s extremity.”

Isaiah 49:7.text: Thus says the Lord who rescued you, Israel’s God: “Sanctify the one who despises his own life, the one abhorred by nations—the slaves of rulers. Kings will see him and rise; rulers will bow to him because of the Lord, for Israel’s Holy One is faithful, and I chose you.”

Isaiah 49:8.text: Thus says the Lord: “At an acceptable time I heard you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. I gave you as a covenant for nations, to establish the earth and inherit a desolate inheritance,

Isaiah 49:9.text: saying to those in bonds, ‘Come out,’ and telling those in darkness to be revealed. They will be fed along all their roads, with pasture along every path.

Isaiah 49:10.text: They will neither hunger nor thirst, nor will scorching heat or the sun strike them. Rather, the One showing them mercy will comfort them and lead them through springs of water.

Isaiah 49:11.text: I will make every mountain into a road and every path into pasture for them.

Isaiah 49:12.text: Behold, these come from afar, these from the north and these from the sea, and others from the Persians’ land.”

Isaiah 49:13.text: Rejoice, heavens, and let earth exult! Let mountains burst out in joy and hills in righteousness, for God had mercy on His people and comforted His people’s lowly ones.

Isaiah 49:14.text: But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”

Isaiah 49:15.text: “Will a woman forget her child, failing to have mercy on the offspring of her belly? Even if a woman forgets these, I will not forget you,” said the Lord.

Isaiah 49:16.text: “Behold, on My hands I painted your walls, and you are before Me continually.

Isaiah 49:17.text: You will swiftly be rebuilt by those who pulled you down, and those who laid you waste will depart from you.

Isaiah 49:18.text: Lift your eyes around and see them all. Behold, they gathered and came to you. As I live, says the Lord, you will put them all on and wrap them around you like a bride’s adornment.

Isaiah 49:19.text: For your deserted, destroyed, and fallen places will now be cramped by inhabitants, and those swallowing you will be removed far from you.

Isaiah 49:20.text: For your sons whom you lost will say within your hearing, ‘This place is too cramped for me. Make room for me, so I can settle.’

Isaiah 49:21.text: You will say in your heart, ‘Who bore these for me? I was childless and widowed. Who raised these for me? I was left alone; where were these of mine?’”

Isaiah 49:22.text: Thus says the Lord: “Behold, I lift My hand toward nations and will raise My signal toward islands. They will bring your sons in their bosom and carry your daughters on shoulders,

Isaiah 49:23.text: and kings will be your foster fathers and ruling women your nurses. They will bow to you upon the earth’s surface and lick the dust of your feet. You will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be ashamed.

Isaiah 49:24.text: Will anyone take spoils from a giant? If someone takes captives unjustly, will he be saved?”

Isaiah 49:25.text: Thus says the Lord: “If someone captures a giant, he will take spoils; one taking from a strong man will be saved. I will judge your case, and I will rescue your sons.

Isaiah 49:26.text: Those who afflicted you will eat their own flesh, drink their own blood like new wine, and become drunk. All flesh will perceive that I am the Lord who rescued you and upholds Jacob’s strength.”

Isaiah 50:1.text: Thus says the Lord: “What is your mother’s divorce document with which I sent her away? Or to which debtor have I sold you? Behold, you were sold because of your sins, and I sent your mother away because of your lawless acts.

Isaiah 50:2.text: Why did I come when no person was there, call when no one obeyed? Is My hand not strong enough to rescue? Am I not able to deliver? Behold, by My threat I will make the sea desolate and turn rivers to deserts; their fish will dry up for lack of water and die in thirst.

Isaiah 50:3.text: I will clothe heaven in darkness and make its covering like sackcloth.”

Isaiah 50:4.text: The Lord gives me a tongue of instruction, to know the right time when a word must be spoken. He appointed morning for me; He added an ear for me to hear,

Isaiah 50:5.text: and the Lord’s instruction opens my ears. I do not disobey or contradict.

Isaiah 50:6.text: I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps. I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.

Isaiah 50:7.text: The Lord became my helper; therefore I was not abashed. Instead, I set my face like solid rock and knew that I would certainly not be ashamed.

Isaiah 50:8.text: For the One who justified me draws near. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him stand against me together. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him approach me.

Isaiah 50:9.text: Behold, the Lord helps me. Who will harm me? Behold, all of you will grow old like a garment, and it will devour you like a moth.

Isaiah 50:10.text: Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to His servant’s voice. Those walking in darkness have no light; trust in the Lord’s name and lean upon God.

Isaiah 50:11.text: Behold, all of you burn fire and strengthen a flame. Walk by your fire’s light and the flame you kindled. These things came to you because of Me; you will fall asleep in sorrow.

Isaiah 51:1.text: “Listen to Me, you who pursue what is right and seek the Lord. Look at the solid rock you quarried and the hollow of the pit you dug.

Isaiah 51:2.text: Look at Abraham your father and Sarah who labored to bear you. He was one, and I called him, blessed him, loved him, and multiplied him.

Isaiah 51:3.text: I will now comfort you, Zion; I have comforted all her deserted places and will make her deserted places like the Lord’s paradise. They will find joy and exultation in her, thanksgiving and a voice of praise.

Isaiah 51:4.text: Listen to Me, listen, My people; and kings, give ear to Me. For law will go out from Me, and My judgment as a light for nations.

Isaiah 51:5.text: My righteousness approaches swiftly, and My salvation will go out like light. Nations will hope in My arm; islands will wait for Me and hope in My arm.

Isaiah 51:6.text: Lift your eyes to heaven and look at earth below. Heaven was made firm like smoke, but earth will grow old like a garment, and earth’s inhabitants will die like these. My salvation will last for ever, and My righteousness will never fail.

Isaiah 51:7.text: Listen to Me, you who know judgment, My people with My law in your heart. Do not fear people’s reproach or be overcome by their contempt.

Isaiah 51:8.text: For a garment will be consumed by time, and wool eaten by a moth. But My righteousness will last for ever, and My salvation through generations of generations.”

Isaiah 51:9.text: Awake, awake, Jerusalem, and clothe yourself with the strength of your arm! Awake as at day’s beginning, as an age-old generation. Are you not the one

Isaiah 51:10.text: who makes the sea desolate, the abundant water of the abyss, who made the sea depths a crossing road for those rescued

Isaiah 51:11.text: and ransomed? For by the Lord they will be brought back and come to Zion with joy and everlasting exultation. Exultation and praise are upon their heads; joy will overtake them. Pain, sorrow, and sighing fled.

Isaiah 51:12.text: “I am, I am the One comforting you. Recognize whom you dreaded and feared: a mortal person, a human being who withered like grass.

Isaiah 51:13.text: You forgot God who made you, who made heaven and founded earth, and feared continually, every day, the face of your oppressor’s anger. For as he planned to remove you—where now is your oppressor’s anger?

Isaiah 51:14.text: For as you are saved, it will not stand or linger.

Isaiah 51:15.text: For I am your God, who stirs the sea and makes its waves resound; the Lord Sabaoth is My name.

Isaiah 51:16.text: I will put My words in your mouth and shelter you under My hand’s shadow, by which I established heaven and founded earth; and He will say to Zion, ‘You are My people.’

Isaiah 51:17.text: Awake, awake, rise, Jerusalem, you who drank the cup of anger from the Lord’s hand. You drank out and emptied the cup of falling, the bowl of anger.

Isaiah 51:18.text: There was no one to comfort you among all your children you bore, and no one to take your hand among all your sons you raised.

Isaiah 51:19.text: These two confront you—who will grieve with you?—fall and crushing, famine and sword. Who will comfort you?

Isaiah 51:20.text: Your sons are helpless, sleeping at every way out like a half-boiled beet, full of the Lord’s anger, exhausted because of the Lord God.

Isaiah 51:21.text: Therefore listen, humbled one, drunk but not from wine.

Isaiah 51:22.text: Thus says the Lord God who judges His people: ‘Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of falling, the bowl of anger. You will not drink it again.

Isaiah 51:23.text: I will throw it into the hands of those who wronged and humbled you, who told your soul, “Bend down, so we may pass.” You laid your back level with the earth, outside for passersby.’”

Isaiah 52:1.text: Awake, awake, Zion! Clothe yourself with your strength, Zion, and put on your glory, Jerusalem, holy city. No uncircumcised and unclean person will pass through you again.

Isaiah 52:2.text: Shake off the dust and rise; sit, Jerusalem. Strip off the bond around your neck, captive daughter Zion.

Isaiah 52:3.text: For thus says the Lord: “You were sold for nothing, and without silver you will be ransomed.”

Isaiah 52:4.text: Thus says the Lord: “My people formerly went down to Egypt to live there as strangers, and they were forcibly led to the Assyrians.

Isaiah 52:5.text: And now, why are you here?” Thus says the Lord. “My people were taken for nothing. Be amazed and wail!” Thus says the Lord. “Because of you, My name is continually blasphemed among the nations.

Isaiah 52:6.text: Therefore My people will know My name on that day, because I am the One speaking. I am present

Isaiah 52:7.text: like beauty on the mountains, like the feet of one proclaiming a report of peace, like one bringing good news. For I will make your salvation heard, saying, ‘Zion, your God will reign.’”

Isaiah 52:8.text: For the voice of those guarding you was raised, and together they will rejoice with their voice. For eyes will see eye to eye when the Lord has mercy on Zion.

Isaiah 52:9.text: Let Jerusalem’s deserted places break out in joy together, for the Lord had mercy on her and rescued Jerusalem.

Isaiah 52:10.text: The Lord will uncover His holy arm before all nations, and all the ends of earth will see the salvation that comes from God.

Isaiah 52:11.text: Depart, depart; go out from there, and do not touch anything unclean. Go out from her midst; separate yourselves, you who carry the Lord’s vessels.

Isaiah 52:12.text: For you will not go out in turmoil or travel in flight, because the Lord will go ahead of you, and the One gathering you is the Lord, Israel’s God.

Isaiah 52:13.text: Behold, My servant will understand, and will be exalted and greatly glorified.

Isaiah 52:14.text: As many will be astonished at you— so your form will be without honour among men, and your glory among men—

Isaiah 52:15.text: so many nations will marvel at him, and kings will close their mouths. For those to whom he was not proclaimed will see, and those who have not heard will understand.

Isaiah 53:1.text: O Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?

Isaiah 53:2.text: We proclaimed before him as a child, as a root in thirsty ground. He has no form nor glory; and we saw him, and he had no form nor beauty.

Isaiah 53:3.text: But his form was without honour, fallen below all men: a man under affliction, and knowing how to bear sickness. For his face has been turned away; he was dishonoured and held of no account.

Isaiah 53:4.text: He bears our sins, and suffers pain for us; yet we reckoned him to be in toil and affliction and distress.

Isaiah 53:5.text: But he was wounded for our iniquities, and has been weakened for our sins. The chastisement of our peace was upon him; by his bruise we were healed.

Isaiah 53:6.text: We all, like sheep, have gone astray; each person has strayed in his own way. And the Lord delivered him over to our sins.

Isaiah 53:7.text: And because he has been afflicted, he does not open his mouth. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb is silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.

Isaiah 53:8.text: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who will declare his generation? For his life is taken from the earth; because of the iniquities of My people he was led to death.

Isaiah 53:9.text: And I will give the wicked in exchange for his burial, and the rich in exchange for his death; for he committed no iniquity, nor was deceit found in his mouth.

Isaiah 53:10.text: And the Lord desires to cleanse him of his affliction. If you give an offering for sin, your soul will see seed that lives long. And the Lord desires to take him away

Isaiah 53:11.text: from the toil of his soul, to show him light and fashion him with understanding, to justify the righteous one who serves many well; and he will bear their sins.

Isaiah 53:12.text: Therefore he will inherit many, and will divide the spoils of the mighty; for his soul was delivered to death, and he was numbered among the lawless. And he bore the sins of many, and for their sins he was delivered up.

Isaiah 54:1.text: “Rejoice, barren woman who does not give birth! Break out and cry aloud, you who do not labor in childbirth, because the deserted woman’s children are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband,” for the Lord has spoken.

Isaiah 54:2.text: “Widen the place of your tent and your curtains. Pitch them; do not spare! Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your pegs.

Isaiah 54:3.text: Spread out still farther to right and left. Your offspring will inherit nations, and you will settle deserted cities.

Isaiah 54:4.text: Do not fear because you were put to shame, or be abashed because you were reproached. For you will forget lasting shame and never remember the reproach of your widowhood.

Isaiah 54:5.text: For the Lord is the One making you; the Lord Sabaoth is His name. The One who rescued you is Himself Israel’s God; He will be called upon throughout all earth.

Isaiah 54:6.text: “The Lord has not called you like an abandoned, fainthearted wife, nor like a wife hated since youth,” says your God.

Isaiah 54:7.text: “For a short time I abandoned you, and with great mercy I will have mercy on you.

Isaiah 54:8.text: In a little anger I turned My face from you, and with everlasting mercy I will have mercy on you,” says the Lord who rescued you.

Isaiah 54:9.text: “This dates for Me from the water in Noah’s time, when I swore to him then concerning the earth not to be angry with you again, nor at a threat against you

Isaiah 54:10.text: for mountains to move away; nor will your hills be shifted. So neither will My mercy toward you fail, nor will your covenant of peace ever be removed.” For the Lord said, “I am gracious to you.”

Isaiah 54:11.text: Humbled and unsettled woman, you were not comforted! Behold, I am preparing carbuncle as your stone and sapphire as your foundations,

Isaiah 54:12.text: and I will make your battlements jasper, your gates crystal stones, and your enclosing wall choice stones,

Isaiah 54:13.text: and all your sons taught by God, and your children in great peace.

Isaiah 54:14.text: You will be built in righteousness. Keep away from injustice, and you will not fear; terror will not approach you.

Isaiah 54:15.text: Behold, newcomers will approach you through Me and take refuge with you.

Isaiah 54:16.text: Behold, I am creating you, not like a smith blowing coals and bringing out an implement for work. I did not create you for ruin, to destroy

Isaiah 54:17.text: every perishable implement. I will not grant success against you. Every voice will rise against you in judgment; you will defeat them all, and those accountable to you will be held liable in it. There is an inheritance for those serving the Lord, and you will be righteous before Me,” says the Lord.

Isaiah 55:1.text: You who thirst, go to the water; and you who have no silver, go and buy wine and rich food, and drink without silver or price.

Isaiah 55:2.text: Why do you pay a price of silver, and give your toil for what does not satisfy? Listen to Me, and you will eat good things, and your soul will delight in good things.

Isaiah 55:3.text: Listen with your ears, and follow My ways; listen to Me, and your soul will live amid good things. And I will make with you an everlasting covenant: the holy and sure blessings of David.

Isaiah 55:4.text: Behold, I have given him as a testimony among the nations, a ruler and commander of nations.

Isaiah 55:5.text: Nations that did not know you will call upon you, and peoples that do not know you will flee to you for refuge, because of your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.

Isaiah 55:6.text: Seek God, and when you find Him, call upon Him; and when He draws near to you,

Isaiah 55:7.text: let the ungodly forsake his ways, and the lawless man his counsels; and let him return to the Lord, and he will receive mercy; for He will abundantly forgive your sins.

Isaiah 55:8.text: For My counsels are not as your counsels, nor are My ways like your ways, says the Lord.

Isaiah 55:9.text: But as the heaven is distant from the earth, so is My way distant from your ways, and your thoughts from My mind.

Isaiah 55:10.text: For as rain or snow comes down from the heaven, and does not return until it has drenched the earth, and made it bring forth and sprout, and given seed to the sower and bread for food,

Isaiah 55:11.text: so it will be with My word, whatever goes out from My mouth: it will certainly not return until all that I have willed is accomplished; and I will prosper your ways and My commandments.

Isaiah 55:12.text: For you will go out in gladness, and in joy you will be taught; for the mountains and the hills will leap, welcoming you with joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their branches.

Isaiah 55:13.text: And the cypress will rise in place of the thorny shrub, and the myrtle will rise in place of the fleabane; and the Lord will be for a name and for an everlasting sign, and will not fail.

Ezra 1:1.text: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, so that the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians. He ordered a proclamation throughout his kingdom, also in writing, saying:

Ezra 1:2.text: “Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build Him a house in Jerusalem in Judea.

Ezra 1:3.text: Who among you belongs to any of His people? His God will be with him, and he will go up to Jerusalem in Judea. Let him build the house of the God of Israel—He is the God in Jerusalem.
